mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last four weekly means (-25.6 to -34.1). This monotone weekly deterioration is a momentum signal: the same decline rate carries forward because the underlying trip-suppression process has not yet found a floor, so the next 28-day mean will be lower than the last.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined in all four weekly means from -25.6 to -34.1
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days, i.e. the four-week decline fails to extend.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT fell 10.9 points week-on-week to -47.0, crossing below the -45 level that in this regime marks a shift from voluntary caution to enforced trip avoidance. Once transit use is that suppressed, discretionary retail trips that depend on rail access collapse within one week, dragging RETAIL_REC to a new low.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 8 points week-on-week and prints below -45
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -36.1 to -47.0 in the final week
failure_condition: In the week after TRANSIT crosses below -45, RETAIL_REC rises or is unchanged versus the prior weekly mean, showing the threshold carries no incremental suppression.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of PARKS at -41.3 and RESIDENTIAL at +17.9 shows households relocating activity from outdoor and out-of-home venues into the home. This substitution is multiplicative rather than additive: when both conditions hold, discretionary retail trips are displaced, so RETAIL_REC keeps falling over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -40 and RESIDENTIAL above +15 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -41.3 while RESIDENTIAL rose to +17.9
failure_condition: When PARKS is below -40 and RESIDENTIAL above +15, mean RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is not lower than mean RETAIL_REC over the prior 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM crossed below zero for the first time in the window (from +0.4 to -5.3), meaning even essential-errand traffic has started to contract. When the most resilient errand category turns negative, the household trip budget is shrinking overall, which removes the residual support that had cushioned discretionary retail, pushing RETAIL_REC lower.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses below 0.0 percent after being non-negative for the prior three weeks
failure_condition: After GROCERY_PHARM turns negative, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or above the prior 14-day mean, indicating essential-trip contraction does not transmit to discretionary retail.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES dropped 19.9 points week-on-week to -45.0, the signature of a work-from-home mandate being newly enforced rather than voluntary caution. Mandated office absence removes commuter-adjacent retail demand and also signals accompanying operating-hour requests to retailers, so RETAIL_REC declines further over a four-week policy horizon.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls more than 15 points week-on-week to a level below -40
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -25.1 to -45.0 in the final week
regime_hint: declared state of emergency with workplace mandates
failure_condition: Following a WORKPLACES drop of more than 15 points to below -40, the 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not lower than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS reading of -41.3 is partly a mid-August holiday-travel effect rather than pure avoidance, since the reference week spans the Obon period when outdoor and park visits are seasonally elevated. As the holiday window closes, that seasonal drag reverses and local shopping traffic partially returns, lifting RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -29.4 to -41.3 in the final weekly mean
regime_hint: post-holiday seasonal normalization in late August
failure_condition: In the two weeks after the holiday period ends, RETAIL_REC does not recover at least 2 points above its final weekly mean of -34.1, showing the PARKS drop was not seasonally driven.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC at -34.1 combined with RESIDENTIAL at +17.9 places the system in a saturated stay-home state: the marginal household has already removed discretionary trips, so further declines require new behavioral withdrawal that is not observable in the proxies. This depletion produces a floor and a partial rebound in the next 14 days.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +15 and RETAIL_REC at or below -34 simultaneously
failure_condition: With RESIDENTIAL above +15 and RETAIL_REC at or below -34, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the prior 14-day mean, showing no saturation floor exists.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES fell together in the final week (-36.1 to -47.0 and -25.1 to -45.0), which is the joint footprint of a newly announced restriction package affecting both commuting and station-area activity. When the two decline in the same week under an active emergency declaration, the retail response is fast and one-week-ahead, so RETAIL_REC falls within the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week by more than 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fell sharply in the final weekly mean
regime_hint: active emergency declaration with joint transit and workplace restrictions
failure_condition: In weeks when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by more than 5 points, the following weekly mean of RETAIL_REC is higher than or equal to the concurrent weekly mean.
